entry_points.text: Slot changes enter arch code before install to veto and build metadata, and after accounting to notify trackers, resize cache and retire old arrays.
Range queries answer uniformity under read protection, cache sizing runs when page totals change, and flag application reconciles logging with access state.

exports.text: Generic layer offers an interval attribute uniformity query, a single-frame attribute read, and a dirty-bitmap mode check.
x86 offers slot validation, commit propagation, slot release, paging-cache sizing, write-track lifecycle, reverse-map allocation and attribute seeding.
Slot-wide operations revoke write access, reduce large mappings toward a target size, and restore large mappings, with per-address-space two-dimensional helpers for the same three tasks.
Remote invalidation covers a guest-frame interval with full fallback plus a whole-slot wrapper.

hazards.text: Relocation with external trackers, guest-memfd slots, over-limit or alias frames, and edge-split, misaligned or mixed huge pages are refused or suppressed.
Tracking setup flushes remotes unconditionally outside the MMU lock; non-writable does not prove unwritable; splits inherit posture and defer invalidation while preserving translation.
Two-dimensional reduction preallocates one table at a time, may abort out of memory with earlier splits installed, and releases raced losers via reclamation.

invariants.text: Staging holds a dedicated mutex and uses a temporary invalid view for removal or relocation with rollback on failure. Disabling logging detaches the bitmap, keeping it reuses storage, enabling allocates word-rounded double bytes and optionally marks all dirty; ring-only suppresses allocation.

Creation and relocation fail with external trackers, over-limit last frames, or direct-bit alias overlap. The limit derives from host width with fallback shifted by page size; alias is nonzero mask overlap.
Reverse-map release walks every paging level, frees each array and clears its pointer.

Attributes live in an indexed array with absent meaning none; only private is advertised when supported. Creation scans contained huge pages bottom-up, clearing mixed when uniform and setting it otherwise; rounding clears low bits to the huge base.
Write-track records allocate once per frame when enabled; a header hook covers removal when disabled.
Oldest-first reclamation skips active roots, batches candidates with restart on unstable walks, then commits and latches the maximum to achieved use.

Two-dimensional protection clears writable on present terminals at or above a minimum size with retry. Children derive with scaled offset, drop size at the smallest size and refresh execution under mitigation. Permission updates preserve access-track encoding; new levels are present writable; linking charges one table page.

Shadow reduction walks largest down toward target; two-dimensional reduction uses parent-before-child in one pass; restoration scans smallest up and invalidates on collapsible discard over the full slot interval.

locks.text: Table install serializes on an arch mutex from copy to publish; whole-slot invalidation needs the outer slots mutex.

Cache changes and shadow walks use exclusive hold with yield and interval flush before yielding; two-dimensional walks use shared hold with allocation outside locks; attribute scans use read protection with retry.

state_machines.text: Removal and relocation go through temporary invalidation, then prepare, kind-specific install and commit; logging on allocates or reuses and counts up, off detaches and counts down.

Tracking off rebuilds large pages; tracking on optionally reduces eagerly then protects and invalidates; cache rests at goal, evicts oldest when over and grows with slot pages unless explicitly sized.

structs.text: Slot state has base frame, page count, flags, dirty bitmap, userspace address and arch area with reverse maps, large-page descriptors and write-track array; machine state has slot locks, page totals, logging count, manual mask, ring config, attribute array, direct bits, cache goals and notifier head.
Paging nodes carry root count with age linkage and shadow counters; consumers link via notifier list; fresh child tables record decremented level, start frame, parent link and ownership marker.

Vocabulary is KVM_MR_CREATE, KVM_MR_DELETE, KVM_MR_MOVE and KVM_MR_FLAGS_ONLY. Flags include KVM_MEM_LOG_DIRTY_PAGES, KVM_MEM_READONLY, KVM_MEM_GUEST_MEMFD, KVM_MEMORY_ATTRIBUTE_PRIVATE and KVM_DIRTY_LOG_INITIALLY_SET. Sizes use PG_LEVEL_4K, PG_LEVEL_2M, KVM_MAX_HUGEPAGE_LEVEL, KVM_NR_PAGE_SIZES, KVM_PAGES_PER_HPAGE, KVM_LPAGE_MIXED_FLAG, KVM_MIN_ALLOC_MMU_PAGES and KVM_MEMSLOT_PAGES_TO_MMU_PAGES_RATIO. Masks use PT_PRESENT_MASK, PT_WRITABLE_MASK, PT_PAGE_SIZE_MASK and SPTE_ENT_PER_PAGE.
